issues.description: The UML in the problem statement specifies addGuestStudents(int): void (i.e., no return value), but the solution implements addGuestStudents(int) returning boolean. The template leaves the method as a TODO (no signature), so students following the UML will implement a void method while the solution/reference uses a boolean return — this mismatch can confuse students about the expected method signature and behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to implement addGuestStudents(int) as void (and update its implementation to simply add the guests or throw/handle invalid input without returning a value), or (B) update the problem statement/UML to indicate a boolean return type and mention the return semantics (e.g., true if addition succeeded, false otherwise). Also update template TODO comment to include the chosen signature so students implement the intended method.
